Consult Summary:
- Adult with known asthma reports 2–3 days of exertional shortness of breath with wheeze and cough; reliever inhaler provides little relief. Clinician suspects a mild asthma exacerbation; advised temporary increase in preventer dose, PRN reliever use with safety-netting, and urgent face-to-face review.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough for 2–3 days.
- Symptom details:
  - Onset/progression: Began 2–3 days ago during a run; persists with brisk walking; not noted at rest. Blue inhaler not helping.
  - Associated symptoms: Wheeze; cough without sputum.
  - Pertinent negatives: No sputum production.
  - Exacerbating factors: Exercise/brisk walking.
  - Relieving factors: Salbutamol (blue inhaler) has not provided relief.
- Asthma control history:
  - Last asthma attack: 3–4 years ago.
  - No prior hospital admissions for asthma.
  - No history of oral steroid use recalled.
  - Last asthma review: ~2 years ago.
  - Baseline peak flow: Patient agreed to “about 380” (units not documented). Has not checked peak flow during current symptoms.
- Current inhaler use:
  - Salbutamol (blue): Using daily and PRN; also using morning/evening to try to prevent symptoms.
  - Preventer inhaler: Using twice daily (name/dose not clearly documented in transcript).
- Allergies: Hay fever; denies medication allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: Historically well-controlled until current episode.
  - Associated medications mentioned:
    - Salbutamol (blue inhaler) – dose/route/frequency not documented beyond “daily and PRN.”
    - Brown preventer inhaler (likely Clenil/beclometasone per clinician) – patient uses twice daily; current dose not clearly documented.
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever): Patient-reported; no treatment discussed.
- Possible eczema: Patient suspects eczema; not formally diagnosed.
  - Associated topical treatments mentioned: Hydrocortisone and emollient (Cetraben mentioned later); see conflict noted under Quality checks.

Social History:
- Physical activity: Recreational running.
- Smoking, alcohol, substances: Not documented.
- Living/occupational factors: Not documented.

Family History:
- Brother: Asthma.
- Sister: Eczema.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented in this consult.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Historical: Baseline peak flow reportedly ~380 (units not documented).
- Patient has not measured peak flow since onset of current symptoms.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected mild asthma exacerbation with suboptimal control over 2–3 days.
  - Plan:
    - Increase brown preventer (Clenil) to 4 puffs twice daily temporarily while awaiting review.
    - Use salbutamol (blue inhaler) as needed up to every 2–4 hours; if requiring this frequency, indicates poor control.
    - Safety-net: If breathing worsens, attend A&E without waiting for GP appointment.
    - Arrange face-to-face GP review within the next few days for chest examination and peak flow assessment.
    - At review, consider need for oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on clinical findings.
- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever).
  - Plan: Not addressed during this consult.
- Issue 3: Possible eczema (patient-reported, not confirmed).
  - Plan: Not addressed during this consult.
- General plan items:
  - Continue using blue inhaler PRN.
  - Temporary increase in inhaled steroid (brown inhaler) as above until reviewed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Vital signs, oxygen saturation.
  - Objective respiratory exam.
  - Confirmed names/doses of all medications; inhaler technique and spacer use; adherence.
  - Peak flow measurement during current episode and personal best with units.
  - Smoking status, alcohol/substance use.
  - Asthma action plan; recent triggers/infections; vaccination status.
  - Allergies list clarification (environmental vs drug).
- Internal conflicts:
  - Preventer/other medications: Patient initially mentioned “Salbutamol, Flanel Bactroban and Hydrocortisone,” then later “Cetraben and Hydrocortisone.” Name “Flanel” likely intended “Clenil” (preventer), but conflict noted regarding Cetraben vs Bactroban; exact preventer name/dose not clearly documented.
  - Allergies: Patient has hay fever but denies medication allergies; no conflict on drug allergy status.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some audio/wording unclear with interruptions and possible mishearing of medication names; several uncertainties documented accordingly.
